evals.prompt: I run a small podcast editing service and want one of those isometric 'how it works' explainer videos for my website. The steps are: book a free call, upload your raw audio, we edit and mix it, you review the cut, and your episode goes live. Mention somewhere that episodes come back in 3 days.
evals.expected_output: Style 3: a 20-second 1920x1080 MP4 with 5 isometric blocks that rise in order, a dot travelling between them, plain-word labels readable on a phone, a stills check at each step, and a report listing files and Done-means checks.
expectations: Video is 20 seconds long (within 0.5 s)
All five steps appear as plain-word labels on screen
The 3-day turnaround is stated on screen
Steps are isometric blocks that rise into place one after another
A dot travels along a path from each block to the next
Labels are readable on a phone (block label text at least 60 px on the 1920-wide frame, about 12 pt upright)
Nothing overlaps or is cut off at the frame edge in the final frame
Avoid list respected: no drop shadows, no neon colours, no floating particles, no camera spin
A still was checked for each of the 5 steps (stills exist and the report refers to them)
Final report lists the files created and confirms each Done-means check

evals.prompt: make a 45 second whiteboard style explainer video about how compound interest works. it's for the intro module of a beginner personal finance course so keep it simple
evals.expected_output: Style 2: a 6-scene script, six black-line SVG drawings (no fills), and a 45-second 1920x1080 MP4 where each drawing animates on stroke by stroke with a short label, and each drawing finishes before the next scene.
expectations: A 6-scene script was written as a file
Six SVG files exist, one drawing per scene
SVG drawings use black lines only, with no colour fills
Video is 45 seconds long (within 0.5 s)
Drawings animate on stroke by stroke (a mid-scene still shows a partial drawing)
Every drawing is complete before the next scene starts
Each scene shows a short label under its drawing
Avoid list respected: no drawing hand, no clip art, no colour fills, one drawing per scene
Final report lists the files created and confirms each Done-means check

evals.prompt: Here's our 2025 monthly signups export: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude-explore/a5730f27-3123-5058-8ba7-92c228ef47de/scratchpad/skill-dev/explainer-video-workspace/inputs/signups-2025.csv - turn it into a short animated chart video I can drop into our investor update.
evals.expected_output: Style 4: a ~30-second MP4 with a title card stating the main finding (November peak, 4,820), a chart type justified in one sentence, numbers counting up to the exact CSV values, the top value highlighted, no pie/3D/legend, and 5 values checked against the CSV.
expectations: Video is about 30 seconds long (25-35 s)
The final message names the chart type with a one-sentence reason
Opens with a title card that states the main finding (November peak of 4,820)
Numbers count up (a mid-build still shows values below their final values)
Every value shown at the end matches the CSV (all 12 months checked from a still)
The top value (November, 4,820) is highlighted
Avoid list respected: no pie chart, no 3D bars, no legend to decode, no gridline on every value
The final message lists at least 5 values checked against the CSV
Final report lists the files created
